did_you_know.text: In the first verse, the LORD is described as a king clothed in majesty and girded with strength, while the world is said to be firmly established and unshakable.
The word “clothed” is repeated in the verse, emphasizing the manifestation of the LORD’s kingship through images of clothing and power.
The verse presents the LORD’s throne as “established”—stable and secure—and connects his reign with the most ancient times: “from of old” and “from eternity.”
The rivers are described as though they were living beings: they raise their voices and lift up their pounding roar—that is, the sound and power of their flow.
The threefold repetition of the word “rivers” emphasizes the power of the waters and the noise they create.
In the fourth verse, the LORD’s power is indirectly compared with the power of the waters: the breakers of the sea are mighty, but the LORD is mightier still and exalted on high.
The expressions “mighty waters” and “the breakers of the sea” create an image of turbulent waters and waves crashing with great force.
At the end of the psalm, the focus shifts from describing the LORD’s kingship and power to his “testimonies,” which are declared to be very trustworthy; his house is described as a holy place.
